sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: The **Tarnished** (褪せ人, *Asebito*; lit. "Faded Ones/People") are a faction in Elden Ring. The player character, the Tarnished, is a member of this group.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown: The Tarnished are individuals who lost the grace of the Erdtree and were consequently banished from the Lands Between by Queen Marika the Eternal. Following the breaking of the Elden Ring, the Tarnished were beckoned by lost grace, fragmentary divine light from the Erdtree, to return.

sections.heading: Background
sections.markdown: In the early age of the Erdtree, Godfrey, the first Elden Lord, fought many battles throughout the Lands Between. He led the War Against the Giants, and defeated the Storm Lord. When his last enemy fell, it is said that the hue of his eyes faded. Queen Marika addressed Godfrey and his warriors as she divested them of their Grace, commanding them to leave the Lands Between and travel to a faraway land, where they would wage war and die. She promised them that, after their deaths, their Grace would be given back, and that they would return to the Lands Between once again, to wage war and brandish the Elden Ring.

sections.heading: The Long March
sections.markdown:
Godfrey and his kinfolk were banished from the Lands Between, beginning an exodus referred to as the Long March. They left their home on boats, although one was said to have been left behind. The warriors who accompanied Godfrey honored him by wielding axes, although Godfrey's own axe was broken in battle during the course of the march. When the Long March came to an end, Godfrey divested himself of kingship and became a simple warrior once more. As Hoarah Loux, he became a chieftain of the Badlands, revered by its bravest warriors.

The Tarnished settled in lands outside the Lands Between, and bore descendants who were also Tarnished. As Queen Marika had commanded them, the Tarnished lived and died in these distant lands.

sections.heading: Return to the Lands Between
sections.markdown:
A long time after the Tarnished left the Lands Between, the Elden Ring was shattered and Queen Marika disappeared. Marika's offspring, the Demigods, claimed shards of the Elden Ring. Tainted by their newfound strength, the Demigods warred in the Shattering, causing the Greater Will to abandon them. With the war yielding no victor, the Guidance of Grace was extended to the Tarnished, who returned from the dead and went back to the Lands Between, guided by Grace. Upon setting foot in the Lands Between once more, the Tarnished received the aid of the Two Fingers, who bid them to seek the Great Runes possessed by the Demigods so as to restore the Golden Order and become Elden Lord. The Tarnished, given life by Grace, gained a form of immortality,, allowing them to return from the dead over and over on their quest to become Elden Lord.

The Guidance of Grace brought together the Tarnished and their Finger Maidens, women in the service of the Two Fingers who were tasked with serving their appointed Tarnished. The Finger Maidens would offer guidance and aid to the Tarnished, as well as turning the Runes they gathered into strength.

sections.heading: Table of Lost Grace
Game events
sections.markdown:
This would change when a Tarnished of no renown crossed the fog and entered the Lands Between. Unlike others, this Tarnished did not meet a Finger Maiden to guide them, but was instead chosen by Torrent, the spectral steed, and Melina, a mysterious woman bound to Grace. Melina provided them with the Sacred Flasks and offered to serve as their maiden, aiding them by turning their Runes into strength. She extended an invitation to the Table of Lost Grace and bestowed the Spectral Steed Whistle to summon Torrent.

This Tarnished gained an audience with the Two Fingers, claimed the Great Runes, and journeyed to the Erdtree to brandish the Elden Ring and become the Elden Lord.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown: Stormveil Castle perches atop a cliff overlooking Limgrave. Currently, it is the stronghold of the Demigod Godrick the Grafted, but long ago it was ruled over by an old king, back when the true storm raged. The castle is heavily guarded and patrolled by Banished Knights, Exile Soldiers, and warhawks with blades grafted to their talons. The exterior of the castle is mottled with craters lined with thorns, which have also spread to the soldiers within. It is said that the source may be hidden deep within the castle.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: , also known as **General Radahn**, the **Red Lion General**, and later as **Promised Consort Radahn** and **Radahn, Consort of Miquella**, is an optional Demigod boss in Elden Ring and a mandatory God boss in Elden Ring:;Shadow of the Erdtree.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown: General Radahn was feared as the strongest Demigod during the Shattering. This Shardbearer must be defeated to access the Realm of Shadow and achieve the "Age of the Stars" ending.

sections.heading: Background
sections.markdown:
Red-maned Radahn was the son of Radagon, a champion of the Erdtree, and Queen Rennala of the Full Moon, head of both the Carian royal family and Academy of Raya Lucaria, born after the Second Liurnian War. He had two siblings, Rykard and Ranni. Radahn inherited his father's flaming red hair and was fond of its heroic implications. From a young age, he was enamored with the Elden Lord Godfrey. Attempting to emulate his idol, Radahn adorned his armor with lions, the symbol of Godfrey and Serosh.

At some point, the first Elden Lord, Godfrey, was robbed of grace and hounded from the Lands Between. Radahn's father, Radagon, left Rennala to become Queen Marika's new consort and the second Elden Lord. Radahn and his siblings were thus raised to demigod status by their new step-mother, Marika.

In their youth, Radahn's Empyrean half-brother Miquella deeply admired him for his kindness and strength, seeing in him the qualities of a lord. When he decided to pursue godhood, he made a vow with Radahn that, upon his deific return, he would take Radahn as his consort. In return, Miquella would uphold some unspecified part of the vow.

Not wanting to abandon his scrawny but beloved steed, Leonard, Radahn studied gravitational magic in Sellia under a master who was an Alabaster Lord. Radahn befriended the Albinauric Gaius, a senior disciple of his teacher, and the two formed a competitive yet friendly rivalry. Radahn's step-brother Messmer the Impaler was also friends with Gaius, and the two became as elder brothers to Radahn.

Mastering gravitational magic allowed Radahn to manipulate the forces of gravity and challenge the stars themselves. During the Starscourge Conflict, Radahn saved Sellia by conquering the stars and arrested their cycles, delaying fate. Having earned himself the moniker "Starscourge," he engraved the gravity crest upon his blades.

Radahn's soldiers were known as the Redmanes for the red-maned lion raising a sword in the image of Radahn on their surcoats. The longest serving of the Redmane Knights was Ogha, who studied gravitational techniques alongside Radahn in Sellia. It was popularly said that the Redmanes knew no weakness. At an unknown period in time, Jerren, a guest of the Carian royals, became a guest commander for Radahn's armies, and they swore a mutual oath of honorable death. During his youth, Radahn witnessed the valor of a gladiator called Freyja, who he asked to become another member of his knights; an offer Freyja accepted.

sections.heading: The Shattering
sections.markdown:
At some point following the Night of Black Knives, Queen Marika shattered the Elden Ring, and her offspring acquired the Great Runes. The maddening taint of their newfound strength led to the Shattering, a war between Marika's demigod descendants, each seeking to become the new ruler of the Lands Between.

From his stronghold of Redmane Castle in the Caelid Wilds, Radahn led his armies against the forces of the other demigods. Radahn tried to challenge Godrick the Grafted in Limgrave, but the latter hid in Stormveil Castle.

By the end of the Shattering, only Radahn and his half-sister Malenia, Blade of Miquella were left standing. The two fought to a stalemate in the Battle of Aeonia, their duel ending inconclusively when Malenia unleashed her Scarlet Rot. As the Scarlet Aeonia flower blossomed, Malenia whispered in Radahn's ear, *"Miquella awaits thee, O promised consort."*

The Scarlet Rot ravaged Caelid and consumed Radahn from the inside, eating away at his psyche but failing to kill him. Following the Battle of Aeonia, Radahn roams the Wailing Dunes as a mindless beast who devours the flesh of friend and foe alike, howling at the sky. Without their commander, the Redmane Knights burned the crest on the left breast of their armor to indicate their resolve not to return home, and to serve as a bulwark against the spread of the rot in Caelid using fire.

Despite his madness, Radahn continues to ride his scrawny steed, as well as halt the motions of the stars. The Radahn Festival has been organized by his men in Castle Redmane to celebrate his last battle. It is a gathering of mighty warriors who might finally put the General out of his misery and claim his Great Rune for themselves. The festival serves as Jerren's way of fulfilling his oath of honorable death to Radahn.

sections.heading: Game events
sections.markdown: Upon the participation of a Tarnished Champion, the Radahn Festival is a success, and Radahn is freed from his tortured existence. His death causes the stars to resume their cycles, some of which come crashing down upon the Lands Between. One such falling star lands in Limgrave, opening the path to Nokron, Eternal City, and allowing the fate of Ranni the Witch to progress.

sections.heading: Shadow of the Erdtree
sections.markdown: Following Radahn's defeat, his soul met its end. However, Miquella sought to revive it, still desiring for Radahn to be his lord consort. Miquella successfully revived Radahn, placing his soul into a vessel made from the remains of Mohg, Lord of Blood, another Demigod slain by the same Tarnished who had defeated Radahn. The Tarnished encounters the newly-resurrected Radahn at the Gate of Divinity at the top of Enir-Ilim. Radahn stands guard as Miquella completes his ascension to godhood and battles the Tarnished once more. During the ensuing battle, Miquella steps out of the Gate of Divinity and embraces Radahn as his consort and fights the Tarnished with Radahn. The Tarnished triumphs over Radahn and Miquella, thus preventing Miquella's age of compassion.

sections.heading: First Encounter (Starscourge Radahn)
sections.markdown:
The fight against Starscourge Radahn only becomes available when the Radahn Festival commences. This requires the player to either activate a Site of Grace in Altus Plateau, talk to Blaidd the Half-Wolf about Radahn in Siofra River, or talk to War Counselor Iji about Jerren.

Torrent can be called during this fight and is useful for closing distance and evading Radahn's ranged attacks.

Multiple NPCs are available to be summoned during the fight, and their summons can be located throughout the arena. Six can be summoned at a time, and once a summon sign is used it will vanish, however each NPC has multiple summon signs that can be used.

The following nine champions are available:

- Alexander, Warrior Jar
- Blaidd the Half-Wolf
- Castellan Jerren (phase 2 only)
- Finger Maiden Therolina
- Great Horned Tragoth
- Knight Leontiel (Tarnished Pack)
- Lionel the Lionhearted
- Okina
- Patches (disconnects after arrival)

sections.heading: Phase 1
sections.markdown:
The player will spawn some distance away from Radahn, with the boss visible at the top of a dune in the distance. Immediately, Radahn will begin firing volleys of arrows which rain down from above, homing in on the player, as well as gravity arrows. The latter can be avoided by hiding behind the clusters of weapons dug into the ground, however the weapons will break when struck. Riding Torrent will make it easier to avoid the volleys. Summon signs can be found in clusters all around the arena, and can be used to summon NPCs to assist in the fight.

Once the player is close enough, Radahn will begin attacking using his swords. He is very mobile, using his horse to cover distance easily. He also uses a number of gravity-based attacks, such as Cragblade, gravity waves, and Collapsing Stars.

sections.heading: Phase 2
sections.markdown: Once his health is below 50%, Radahn will launch himself into the sky, disappearing for several seconds. He will then come crashing down in a ball of fire, dealing devastating damage to anyone caught in the impact. Radahn now gains the ability to raise four floating rocks, which will hover beside him and then launch at the player or their summons. He also gains the ability to float into the air and spin rapidly while charging.

sections.heading: Environment
sections.markdown: The Wailing Dunes is a very large arena consisting of many tall dunes, with Radahn initially standing at the top of the largest dune close to the centre of the area. Clusters of weapons can be found stuck in the sand, and can be used to hide from Radahn's arrows. Summon signs can be found throughout the arena, often in clusters of two or three.

sections.heading: Strategy
sections.markdown: - During the first encounter, Radahn can be defeated by luring him to the cliffs in the far north, causing him to fall to his death. Alternatively, players can position themselves at the southern shore during his phase transition, leading Radahn to crash into the ocean upon descent.

sections.heading: Second Encounter (Promised Consort Radahn)
sections.markdown: The second encounter with Radahn serves as the final boss of the *Elden Ring: Shadow of the Erdtree* expansion. The first phase is **Promised Consort Radahn** and the second is **Radahn, Consort of Miquella**.

sections.heading: Phase 1
sections.markdown:
Just like in the base game, players will spawn a distance away from Radahn. While retaining his gravity magic, and as his soul now possessed Mohg's remains, Radahn now employs Bloodflame, and seamlessly switches between the two elemental magics while in combat. To defeat him, it is always important to time your attacks in between Radahn's string of attacks or pull off counters at the very end of a combo. Because of his recovery time, this makes his boss battle complicated, as he can launch other attacks almost instantly after finishing a heavy attack. As a result, it is important to note that patience and appropriate timing are the keys to defeating Radahn. The optimal moment to attack is when he finished his basic sword combos, and would take a brief pause to recover.

At the start of his boss battle, he will nearly always use a gravity attack to prevent players from summoning or buffs upon entry into the boss battle. Because of this, players are recommended to use buffs before accessing the boss and cast summons right after dodging the initial attack. During his first phase, Radahn will use a flurry of combos aside from special abilities such as a Bloodflame Slash and his Gravity attacks. After being reduced to 65% of his health, this will trigger a cutscene leading to Phase 2.

sections.heading: Phase 2
sections.markdown:
In this phase, Radahn's previous attacks are improved and he gains new powerful abilities. Most of them are Holy-powered and have a wider AoE. Overall, while his attacks become more lethal, Radahn is now faster in speed, now capable of creating mirror images to attack and using strong Holy-based abilities, making the boss battle more difficult and challenging. However, despite gaining immense power, Radahn's health has already been reduced to 75%, allowing players to gain a slight edge. It is important to capitalize on the pauses of Radahn's combo attacks, as there are opportunities to strike. Constantly taking advantage of them can deplete his health and because Radahn's attacks can be very punishing if caught off-guard, you have to be prepared to switch between offensive and defensive at times.

While Radahn can still perform similar combos from Phase 1, they have an additional Holy damage explosion at the end. As Miquella is now mounted on his back, he can do a grab attack where he will glow and jump at the player in order to grab them. If successful, Radahn will bring them close to Miquella, who will then place the player under a charm. While this doesn't deal any damage, if Radahn successfully grabs the player a second time while they are charmed, this will ultimately result in instant death. Using Miquella's Great Rune will undo the charm.

sections.heading: Environment
sections.markdown: The arena consists of a very wide area, with a rough white surface filled with gray-white decomposed corpses, which can be found sticking from the ground. At the other end of the arena, stands the Gate of Divinity itself, where Miquella will step out in divine aspect in the second phase.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- General Radahn and his foot soldiers engaged Margit, the Fell Omen during an undisclosed battle of the Shattering.
- Starscourge Radahn's feet have been eaten away by the scarlet rot.
- Promised Consort Radahn has Omen horns and casts Blood Oath Incantations because he inhabits Mohg's body.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.markdown:
- Radahn is the only Shardbearer boss with no spoken dialogue or cinematic introduction immediately before his battle (excluding the cutscene triggered by speaking with Castellan Jerren) or during his phase transition.
 - Although Radahn remains silent in the DLC, unused voice lines suggest he once had an introductory monologue.
- The description of the Longtail Cat Talisman referenced Radahn owning a pet cat, though this detail was later removed.
- Hidetaka Miyazaki has cited Radahn's first battle as his personal favorite boss fight, praising the character's design and the duel's bittersweet tone.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Sorcerer Rogier** is an NPC in Elden Ring. He is first encountered as an optional summon against Margit, the Fell Omen, and is later found within a church searching for knowledge in Stormveil Castle.

sections.heading: Background
sections.markdown:
A Tarnished dedicated to investigating the fateful Night of Black Knives, Rogier familiarized himself with D, Hunter of the Dead and Fia, Deathbed Companion at the Roundtable Hold. He and Fia discussed at length the Black Knifeprints left by the Black Knife Assassin. He hasn't seen the Guidance of Grace for a long time.

He later left the Hold to search for clues at Stormveil Castle, where he offered to teach the Tarnished his magical combat arts, warning them of Godrick's Tarnished hunters. While exploring the lower reaches of the castle, Rogier discovered a cadaver of the Prince of Death and was infected with Death Blight.

Back at the Roundtable and immobilized by his condition, Rogier imparted his knowledge of the plot and Those Lost in Death to the Tarnished. If Rogier receives a Black Knifeprint from the Tarnished, he deduces that the one who enchanted the assassins' weapons was Ranni the Witch. He urges the Tarnished to seek Ranni and enter her service in order to learn more. However, he soon succumbs to the Deathroot, leaving behind a note informing the Tarnished of the whereabouts of D's inseparable twin, Devin.

Fia later summons Rogier as one of her Champions at the Prince of Death's Throne in Deeproot Depths.

1. Roundtable Hold
 - Meet him at Roundtable Hold after defeating Godrick. Tell him that you have defeated Godrick and then ask about the corpse below Stormveil.
 - Speak to Fia to learn about the Black Knifeprint.
1. Black Knife Catacombs
 - Obtain the Black Knifeprint from the wounded Black Knife Assassin in Black Knife Catacombs in Liurnia.
1. Roundtable Hold
 - Give Rogier the Black Knifeprint.

 - Reload the area and speak to Rogier. He will ask you to investigate Ranni.
1. Three Sisters (Ranni's Rise)
 - Head to Ranni's Rise and speak to Ranni. She will be dismissive and ask you to leave.
1. Roundtable Hold
 - Return to Roundtable Hold and tell Rogier about Ranni. He will ask that you enter her service to further the investigation.

 - Return to Ranni's Rise and agree to serve Ranni.
1. Roundtable Hold
 - Return to Roundtable Hold and speak to Rogier. He will tell you that his condition is worsening.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Sorceress Sellen** is a merchant NPC in Elden Ring. She is initially found in Waypoint Ruins in Limgrave and is eager to share her glintstone sorceries.

sections.heading: Background
sections.markdown:
Sellen was considered to be the most promising glintstone sorceress to ever attend the Academy of Raya Lucaria. Her first teacher at the academy was the sorcerer Azur, one of the founding glintstone sorcerers and originator of the Karolos Conspectus. Azur, along with Lusat, was banished from the academy due to their study of the Primeval Current, a study Sellen wished to pursue. However, following accusations of unspeakable treatment of her fellow scholars under the name of the Graven Witch, Sellen too was expelled from the academy. Sellen had sought to restore the Primeval Current, desiring glintstone sorceries unbound by terrestrial taboos and the pedantry of the Carian Royal Family.

Sellen was also an acquaintance of Preceptor Seluvis, and a frequent visitor to his underground cellar, where he kept his collection of puppets. When Sellen was expelled, Seluvis helped her in some capacity, for which she owes him.

At some point following her banishment, Sellen was imprisoned in Witchbane Ruins on the Weeping Peninsula, bound by the Academy's shackles. She managed to manifest a projection of herself in the Waypoint Ruins in Limgrave. It is here that she meets the Tarnished, who becomes her apprentice, learning glintstone sorceries from her. When she learns that the Tarnished has found Master Azur on Mt. Gelmir, she requests that they seek out Master Lusat, speculating that he returned to his home of Sellia, Town of Sorcery. The Tarnished discovers Lusat, in a near-inorganic state much like Azur, in Sellia Hideaway, and reports back to Sellen.

sections.heading: Freeing Sellen
sections.markdown:
Much like Ranni the Witch, Sellen's fate is tied to the stars, and with the defeat of Starscourge Radahn, Sellen becomes dispossessed of her immortality. This makes her a target of Jerren, a friend of the Carian Royal Family who once made a promise to exterminate the witch. Sellen reveals to the Tarnished that the form they have been speaking to is a projection, and that her true body resides in Witchbane Ruins. The Tarnished meets with Sellen's true body, shackled in the ruin's cellar, and she asks them to remove her Primal Glintstone, beseeching them to look after it. Jerren arrives to find Sellen's previous body already perished. The Tarnished later places Sellen's Primal Glintstone into a puppet in Seluvis's basement, which bears a striking resemblance to Sellen's old body.

Sellen, now in her new, more youthful body, returns to the Academy and displaces Rennala, Queen of the Full Moon. She has the bodies of Azur and Lusat moved back to the Academy, so that she can finally hone the Primeval Current. She offers her support to the Tarnished in their mission to become Elden Lord, and requests that when the time comes, they illuminate her about the secrets of life which course the Elden Ring Before long, however, Jerren finally catches up to her. Should the Tarnished aid her in beating back Jerren, she will continue her research. When the Tarnished next sees her, she has transformed into a Graven Mass.

sections.heading: Questline progression
sections.markdown:
1. Waypoint Ruins
 - Sellen can be found in the cellar of Waypoint Ruins after defeating the Mad Pumpkin Head. Talk to Sellen and then select "I wish to learn glintstone sorceries" to receive the "Nod in Thought" Gesture, and to unlock her sorcery shop.
 - *(Optional)* If the Radahn Festival has not commenced, Sellen will have dialogue about it if you have Seluvis's Introduction in your inventory. This is obtained by progressing Blaidd the Half-Wolf's questline and speaking to Seluvis about Nokron prior to initiating the Festival.
1. Waypoint Ruins
 - Find Primeval Sorcerer Azur, located beyond the Hermit Village on Mt. Gelmir, to obtain Comet Azur. Return to Sellen and select the "Show Azur's Sorcery" dialogue option. After listening to this dialogue, select the "Tell me your story" option, and then select "Let us journey together". Next, select "I have a favor to ask" to obtain the Sellian Sealbreaker.
 - The Sellian Sealbreaker can be used to open a sealed tunnel in Sellia Hideaway, behind which is Primeval Sorcerer Lusat. Interact with him to receive Stars of Ruin. It is now possible to select the "Lusat's location" dialogue option when talking to Sellen, which will reward you with a Starlight Shards. This option can be avoided until later in the questline.
1. Witchbane Ruins
 - After Starscourge Radahn has been defeated, talk to Sellen to learn that her true body is in Witchbane Ruins. Travel there and speak to the shackled Sellen to obtain Sellen's Primal Glintstone.
 - Reload the area and return to find Castellan Jerren. In order for him to appear, you must have spoken to him in Redmane Castle after defeating Starscourge Radahn.
1. Three Sisters
 - Travel to the Three Sisters and go to the ruined structure north-east of Ranni's Rise. Roll or attack the ground to reveal a hidden staircase leading to a basement full of immobile puppets. Pass through the illusory wall on the far end of the room to find a puppet duplicate of Sellen. Interact with the puppet to insert Sellen's Primal Glintstone, resurrecting Sellen in her new body.
1. Academy of Raya Lucaria
 - There will now be two summon signs outside the door to the Raya Lucaria Grand Library; one red and one gold. To progress Sellen's questline, select the gold summon sign. You will be summoned as a co-operator to assist Sellen in defeating Witch-Hunter Jerren. Defeat Jerren to receive the Eccentric's Set.
 - This step can only be completed if Rennala, Queen of the Full Moon has been defeated.
1. Academy of Raya Lucaria
 - After defeating Jerren, Sellen can be found where Rennala is usually based. Speak to her to receive the Glintstone Kris. If you have not done so already, find Primeval Sorcerer Lusat in Sellia Hideaway and speak to Sellen to select "Lusat's location" and receive Starlight Shards.
 - It is also possible to obtain Azur and Lusat's armour sets by returning to their respective locations at this point.
1. Academy of Raya Lucaria
 - Reload the area after telling Sellen about Lusat. Sellen, now in the form of a Graven Mass, can be found to the side of the room. The Witch's Glintstone Crown can be obtained here. It is still possible to purchase sorceries from her and to offer her scrolls.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Portraits of Sellen are hung around the Academy of Raya Lucaria, notably the Debate Parlor.
- Sellen may be summoned as a cooperator against the Red Wolf of Radagon if her Primal Glintstone has been inserted in the doll body from Seluvis's Cellar. Given that this requires both reaching the top of Mt. Gelmir and defeating Starscourge Radahn before you have made significant progress in the Academy of Raya Lucaria, this is rather unlikely to happen naturally.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.markdown:
- Sellen's body in the Waypoint Ruins and the doll body in Seluvis's cellar have some differences, with the doll body having a smaller head as well as paler skin and its hair is brown instead of the original's black hair.
- Per the description of the Primal Glintstone Blade, sorcerers would slice open their hearts to imbue primal glintstone with their soul, killing them. As Sellen is already in possession of a Primal Glintstone, it is possible that she has already died, and that the body imprisoned in Witchbane Ruins is not her original body.
- Both Sellens in Limgrave are protected by enemies that bring down a cascade of energy. The Miranda Blossom at Waypoint Ruins calls down Holy light, while the Graven Mass at Witchbane Ruins triggers a cascade of starry Magic.

sections.heading: Acquisition

Alternatively, use one of the Wandering Mausoleums with a bell to duplicate one (can only obtain one per playthrough using either method).

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Has a 30% damage bonus against Gravity-affinity enemies.
- Scales best with Strength until it reaches 54, where after Dexterity-scaling becomes more effective until it reaches 40. Intelligence-scaling is mostly irrelevant for weapon damage.
- Despite being paired weapon it still receives the 50% Strength-bonus from two-handing.

 - Since both Magic damage and Fire damage have specialized ways to increase their damage (their respective Shrouding Cracked Tear, as well as Terra Magica for Magic and Flame, Grant Me Strength for Fire) it may be best to think ahead and try to specialize if you are about to challenge a touch foe or boss.
- One of the main weaknesses of this weapon is the relative lack of other equipment that scales well with both Intelligence and Faith, which pretty much only the Golden Order Seal being a strong option. The Prince of Death's Staff (and the much harder to get Gelmir Glintstone Staff) has rather subpar returns for Sorcery Scaling when the two stats are below 60, making it only relatively good with Death Sorceries and rather bad with everything else.
- It's possible to invest primarily in only one of the two stats, but it's ill-advised to do this beyond the early and early-to-mid sections of the game. This is because, while doing so lets you potentially hyper-specialize in one of the attacks and more easily overcome flat defences early on, it will also lock you into one element, and both the sword's own damage and the skill's damage doesn't scales all that well past 54 in the associated stat.
- Just meeting the sword's requirements means that you will have the Intelligence to cast the Magic-boosting Terra Magic and the Fire-boosting Flame, Grant Me Strength, and just 1 more points in Faith will let the wielder cast the Golden Vow spell (which also boosts the skill since it's based of weapon Attack Power).

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: The **Scholar** is a character in Elden Ring Nightreign, one of the two playable Nightfarer classes included in the DLC.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
Scholar is the perfect choice for a precise and technical playstyle. He specializes in crowd control, debuffs, and team utility, making him especially valuable in coordinated group play.

Scholar favors Thrusting Swords, which focus on pokes, counters, and spacing rather than brute force, and they synergize extremely well with his presumed reliance on Arcane as his highest stat. His movement also appears more refined than most Nightfarers, incorporating smooth sidesteps, backstep feints, and flowing motion chains that allow him to control distance while maintaining pressure.

Much like the Executor, Scholar appears to benefit heavily from status effects—however, he applies them differently. For example, pairing his Arcane scaling with a weapon like the Antspur Rapier (which applies Scarlet Rot) could lead to highly efficient status infliction across multiple enemies, especially when combined with his unique skills.

sections.heading: Stats
sections.markdown: Stats displayed below are for character at level 15.

sections.heading: Passive Ability
sections.markdown:
Bagcraft — *"Store additional resources. Level up the power or effect of items by using them."*

Increased item stack limit for consumable Tools, which can be leveled up twice during an Expedition. The Scholar can level up items by repeatedly using the item. Leveling up doesn't focus on individual items but instead on the item category. For example, if a player frequently uses a throwable pot, all throwable pots will benefit from the effect.

Increased stack limits for consumable Tools, which can be upgraded twice during an Expedition. The Scholar upgrades items through repeated use, and upgrades apply to the whole item category. If a player often uses a Throwing Pot, every Throwable Pot becomes stronger.
Bagcraft**
- Item-handling level up [2] - Improves the effectiveness.
- Item-handling level up [3] - Adds a secondary effect to the item.

sections.heading: Character Skill
sections.markdown:
Analyze — *"Study your enemies. The longer you observe, the better your combat advantage."*

The Scholar's awareness and ability to make observations on the battlefield are his primary strengths. **Analyze** applies debuffs to enemies and buffs to himself and nearby allies. Activating the ability creates a large circle that marks all targets inside it. Focusing on a target triggers a red gauge that fills over time; the longer the analysis, the stronger the resulting buff or debuff. Once the indicator is complete, press the assigned button to apply the effect.

Analysis speed is distance-based: close targets fill quickly, while distant ones take longer. The Scholar is exposed during this process because he lowers his weapon, so the skill is safest to use when enemies are not pressuring him.

- Best used when multiple targets are lined up on-screen, including enemies and allies.
Analyze Buff and Debuff Effects**
- Level 1 Buff - Increased Stamina
- Level 3 Buff - Conjure a shield that releases a shockwave when hit.
- Level 1 Debuff - Decreases attack.
- Level 3 Debuff - Take extra damage on the next hit received.

sections.heading: Ultimate Art
sections.markdown:
Communion — *"Taboo Knowledge: Damage is shared by linked enemies and can heal threaded allies."*

The Scholar's ultimate ability binds together all nearby foes and allies in an area of effect. Any damage inflicted on one linked enemy is mirrored across all others. For allies, each connected member benefits from any single source of healing.

- The Scholar is invulnerable to damage while casting Communion.
- Most effective against clustered enemies and multi-target bosses to enhance both damage output.
- Most effective when cast on both allies, significantly boosting team survivability.

sections.heading: Background
sections.markdown:
]]

A blessing believed to have invited riches, silver was valued in the Lands Between for its practical and mystical properties. It was used by many factions to forge a wide range of armor, weapons, and sacred objects throughout the ages.

The Nox of the Eternal Cities used silver to create artificial lifeforms. Silver Tears were formless creatures that mimicked objects and other living things. Although their liquid metal bodies could be tempered into flowing weapons, silver tears had wills of their own. Like Silver Tears, Albinaurics were arcane creatures that possessed silvery cores housing their life essence.

Silver mist also had life-sapping properties, as utilized by Nox Nightmaidens.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Terra Magica** is a spell in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.markdown: Creates a large, stationary sigil inside of a circle, centered on where the caster stands that lasts for 30 seconds and grants a +35% (+20% in PvP) increase to all Magic damage dealt while standing inside of it.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
Since all Magic damage, not only that from Sorceries, is increased, other powerful sources of Magic damage such as the incantation Glintstone Breath and the unique skill Sorcery of the Crozier from the Watchdog's Staff Colossal Weapon benefit greatly from it.

The buff is unique, meaning it stacks with any other buff used. Additionally, since the buff only matters at the time the damage is inflicted, the damage increase is granted even if the spell, skill, or consumable is used outside of the affected area as long as the caster stands in the sigil when it hits.

Due to the limited area of effect where the buff is granted it can be difficult to make use of the effect except in ambushes and the starting moments of a fight.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.markdown:
- The ground-bound sigil of this is Sorcery is the same as the one created when casting basic Glintstone Sorceries such as Glintstone Pebble and Glintstone Arc.
- This spell's name was Terra Magicus upon release but was changed to Terra Magica at a later date.
- The buffs is applied through what is basically an attack that deals 0 damage, as can be seen if the Golden Epitaph unique skill Last Rites is used in the vicinity of an already created Terra Magica. This is because the unique skill grants a small amount of flat Holy damage which Terra Magica thereafter applies on each attack.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Sorcerer Thops** is an NPC in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
A former student of the Academy of Raya Lucaria, Thops was considered a "bluntstone", lacking any talent for sorcery, yet he looked up to Sorceress Sellen prior to her expulsion from the Academy.

When the Shattering broke out, the Academy declared that they would not interfere with the conflict, and the scholars cast repelling seals on the gates. Thops was outside the Academy's grounds when the seals were cast, and thus found himself unable to return.

Thops encounters the Tarnished at the Church of Irith in Liurnia of the Lakes, just beyond Stormveil Castle. He offers to share his limited knowledge of sorceries with them in return for a small donation, and advises them to seek out an Academy Glintstone Key so that they can access the Academy of Raya Lucaria. Should the Tarnished find a second Glintstone Key, they may offer it to Thops, allowing him to finally return to the Academy. sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Stats and Attributes** determine the player character's gameplay-relevant properties. They can be inspected at the Character Status page, where the game separates them into the following categories:

sections.heading: Attributes
sections.markdown: These are the 8 attributes that can be increased by leveling up. Some affect base stats.

sections.heading: Attack Power
sections.markdown:
Depending on the weapon or shield wielded, a specific type of damage is done.

Note that Attack Power and damage dealt is not the same thing, with the latter depending how the former compares with defense. More specifically, if Attack Power is more than eight times as large as defense then damage dealt is equal to 90% of Attack Power while if Attack Power is less than an eighth of defense damage dealt is equal to 10% of Attack Power. If Attack Power is in between these breakpoints damage dealt falls somewhere between these two numbers.

sections.heading: Guard Damage Negation
sections.markdown: A weapon or shield's ability to reduce incoming damage when blocking.

sections.heading: Damage Negation
sections.markdown: Damage Negation** (obtained through armor or items) reduces the damage of incoming attacks. Each Damage Type has a corresponding defense stat and damage negation stat that governs its mitigation.

sections.heading: Defense
sections.markdown: Defense** (obtained through stats) also reduces the damage of incoming attacks.

sections.heading: Resistances
sections.markdown: Determine the character's defense against Status Effects. Can by increased by armors, Talismans, and items.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Tanith, Volcano Manor Proprietress** is an NPC in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
Tanith is the consort of Praetor Rykard and the leader of the Recusants, a band of Tarnished who have taken up arms against the Erdtree and vowed to hunt down their own kind. She sits on a throne in the Volcano Manor, located on the summit of Mt. Gelmir.

When Tanith first met Rykard, she was working as a dancer in a foreign land, but soon she became his consort. She became truly charmed by Rykard when he swore himself to blasphemy, being the only human to remain by his side when he was devoured by the great serpent, even refusing to imbibe a Tonic of Forgetfulness offered to her by Rykard, believing there to be no greater distress than to forget him.

Tanith is the adoptive mother of Rya, although Rya believes her to be her true mother, having been told that she was born of the grace of a glorious king. Although they are not biologically related, Tanith professes to care for Rya, whose true name is Zorayas.

The Tarnished first meets Tanith in the entrance chamber of Volcano Manor, accompanied by her Crucible Knight bodyguard, where she offers them the opportunity to join the Recusants. Should the Tarnished accept, they are tasked with hunting down several other Tarnished. After tracking down and killing two Tarnished, Tanith divulges the truth about Volcano Manor, and about Rykard, Lord of Blasphemy.

After the Tarnished slays Rykard, Tanith thanks them, as their victory proved Rykard to yet be weak. She announces that she will leave Volcano Manor, however she instead moves to Rykard's audience chamber, where she can be found devouring the corpse of her lord, wishing to become his serpent so that they can devour the gods together.

sections.heading: Questline Progression
sections.markdown:
Defeating Rykard, Lord of Blasphemy at any point during Tanith's questline will cause all subsequent steps in the questline to become locked.#Upon entering Volcano Manor, Tanith can be found to the right of the Site of Grace. Speak to her and agree to join the family. Tanith will give you the Drawing Room Key.
1. Go into the corridor to the right of Tanith and open the first door on the left. Pick up the Letter from Volcano Manor on the table as well as the Recusant Finger.
1. Travel to the entrance to the colosseum in Stormhill and interact with the invasion sign to fight Old Knight Istvan. After defeating him, report back to Tanith to obtain Magma Shot.
1. Go back to the drawing room and pick up the Letter from Volcano Manor. Travel to Altus Plateau and find an invasion sign at the bottom of the gorge leading to Shaded Castle. Interact with the sign to fight Rileigh the Idle. After defeating him, talk to Tanith to obtain the Serpentbone Blade.
1. *(Optional)* If you have advanced Rya's questline and met her in serpent form, and rested at a Site of Grace in the main dungeon area of Volcano Manor, speak to Tanith to obtain the Tonic of Forgetfulness. This step will be locked if you kill Juno Hoslow, Knight of Blood, before giving Rya the Serpent's Amnion.
1. Pick up the Red Letter from the drawing room, and travel to the Shack of the Lofty in the Mountaintops of the Giants. Interact with the invasion sign to fight Juno Hoslow, Knight of Blood. Report back to Tanith to obtain the Taker's Cameo.
1. Tanith will now offer to send you directly to Rykard, Lord of Blasphemy, bypassing the rest of the Volcano Manor. Defeat Rykard and return to Tanith and exhaust her dialogue.
1. Travel to the Rykard, Lord of Blasphemy Site of Grace to find Tanith eating the remains of Rykard.
1. *(Optional)* After obtaining the Dancer's Castanets from Patches in Shaded Castle, offer them to Tanith. There is no reward for doing so, however the Dancer's Castanets will be removed from your inventory.
1. *(Optional)* Attacking Tanith will cause her to die in a single hit. You will then be invaded by Tanith's Knight. Defeating the knight will reward you with Aspects of the Crucible: Breath and the Consort's Set.

Constructed by the civilization that created the imps, catacombs, and Stonesword Keys, the great Belfries are adorned with baldachins and images of the nameless bearded god of the Ancient Dynasty. They are protected by Headless Troll Knights, not unlike the Mausoleum Knights who guard the Wandering Mausoleums.

Three of the belfries host Sending Gates which will allow access to remote regions of the Lands Between, and must be unlocked using Imbued Sword Keys. One such key can be found in a treasure chest at the foot of the northernmost belfry.

A sign is posted outside each sending gate, teasing its destination. The sending gates lead to these locations:

- Chapel of Anticipation (*"Precipice of Anticipation"*): The area where the game began. The player may return to defeat the Grafted Scion if they did not at the start, as well as obtain The Stormhawk King and Stormhawk Deenh.
- Crumbling Farum Azula (*"Crumbling Lands"*): An isolated section of Farum Azula, where the player may obtain a Pearldrake Talisman.

Before it was the scarlet rot Swamp of Aeonia, the heart of Caelid contained the Street of Sages, a western extension of Sellia, Town of Sorcery, where great sorcerers practiced Gravity Sorcery. Alongside peers Gaea and Gaius, young Radahn learned this potent form of magic from an ancient Alabaster Lord. However, it was fate that the stars would destroy Sellia. After learning all he could from his master, Radahn confronted the stars and prevailed. Following the Starscourge Conflict, the Red Lion was the renowned Starscourge.

The area was later known as the site of the last battle of the Shattering—the Battle of Aeonia. The Redmane forces of General Radahn clashed the invading cleanrot forces of Miquella of the Haligtree. The mightiest Demigods and greatest champions of the era—Starscourge Radahn and Malenia, Blade of Miquella fought each other to a standstill. Unable to match Radahn's measure, Malenia snapped the Unalloyed Gold Needle that suppressed her curse, producing her first-ever bloom of her Scarlet Aeonia. She unleashed her Aeonian Butterflies and gained wings of strength.

In the aftermath, Miquella himself rescued Redmane Freyja, who was striken with rot. He drained the disease from her body, earned her loyalty, and vanished, abandoning Commander O'Neil, Malenia, and her Cleanrot army. Over time, the area was scarlet rot formed a vast red bog that gave rise to ancient Rot Disciples and contemporary Kindred of Rot. A great scarlet rotflower tree grew, and rot ate away at the land like a vicious plague. Later, young Scarlet Buds, offshoots of Malenia, were born of the rot. sections.heading: The Night of Black Knives
sections.markdown:
During the Golden Age of the Erdtree, a fragment of the Rune of Death was stolen by Lunar Princess Ranni, who used it to forge godslaying Black Knives. These knives were used by the Black Knife Assassins who, one night, entered Leyndell and assassinated Godwyn the Golden. As the assassins fled the capital, an assassin named Tiche was killed protecting her mother Alecto, the leader of the assassins.

Ranni slew body at the moment of Godwyn's death, causing the Cursemark to break into two half-wheels rather than form a circle. While Ranni died in the flesh, Godwyn's soul alone perished, sentencing him to live in death. His body was interred in the Erdtree's roots beneath Leyndell, where it mutated and warped. Later, the Rune of Death began to spread through the roots in the form of Deathroot, giving rise to Those Who Live in Death.

In preparation for the fallout of the Night of Black Knives, earlier that same night, Ranni met with her elder brother and co-conspirator, Praetor Rykard. She gifted him a slab of rock inscribed with traces of the Rune of Death, which was to serve as a last-resort foil to Maliketh, the Black Blade, in case a battle between Rykard and Maliketh came to pass.

sections.heading: The Shattering of the Elden Ring
sections.markdown:
The Night of Black Knives became the catalyst for the Shattering. In response to Godwyn's death, Queen Marika the Eternal used her hammer to shatter the Elden Ring. Elden Lord Radagon, her other half, attempted to repair the Elden Ring, but in vain. As punishment for her offense, Marika (alongside Radagon) was imprisoned within the Erdtree.

Consequently, the shattering of the Elden Ring corrupted the Golden Order, and led to a Great War that would leave the Lands Between in ruin.

sections.heading: The Shardbearers
sections.markdown:
The shards of the Elden Ring, known as Great Runes, were inherited by Marika's Demigod offspring. Tainted by the strength of the Great Runes, the Demigods warred, with the conflict becoming known as the Shattering.

Morgott, a Demigod of the Golden Lineage who was born as a graceless Omen, inherited a Great Rune known as the anchor ring which houses the base, proving his pedigree as a member of the Golden Lineage and as the Lord of Leyndell. Taking on the moniker of the "veiled lord", Morgott ruled over Leyndell, slaughtering countless champions in defence of the Erdtree under the guise of Margit, the Fell Omen.

Praetor Rykard, whose noble ambitions had turned to gluttonous depravity, fed himself to the blasphemous serpent after obtaining his Great Rune. His consort, Tanith, established the recusants of Volcano Manor, waging a war against the Erdtree in his stead.

Godrick, a distant relation of Marika whose blood was sorely diluted, escaped the capital by hiding amongst the womenfolk, bringing with him a multitude of treasures including the Mimic's Veil. He hid from General Radahn in Stormveil Castle, and later insulted Malenia, only to grovel for mercy after he himself was defeated at her hands. He turned to the act of grafting in order to attain power, so that one day he could return to the capital.

General Radahn, famed as the scourge of the stars, led the Redmane Knights during the Shattering. They were met in battle by Malenia, Blade of Miquella, and her undefeated army of Cleanrot Knights. They fought to a standstill, until Malenia unleashed her Scarlet Rot, ending the duel inconclusively. Radahn was driven mad by the rot and was forced to wander the battlefield as a mindless beast, devouring the corpses of those who died during the conflict, whether they be a friend or foe. Malenia, who became comatose, was carried back to the Haligtree of her brother Miquella by Cleanrot Knight Finlay, one of the few survivors of the battle.

Ranni, the instigator of the Night of Black Knives, is said to have cast aside her Great Rune, and its present whereabouts are unknown.

Mohg, known only as the Lord of Blood, began building his dynasty underground in secret. To this end he abducted Miquella from his resting place in the Haligtree, wishing to raise the Empyrean to full godhood and become his consort.However, Miquella never responded to Mohg, no matter how hard the omen tried, and continued to remain asleep in his cocoon.

sections.markdown:

The First Defense of Leyndell was precipitated by the deterioration of a sovereign alliance. Godefroy the Grafted was captured by Ancient Dragon Knight Kristoff during this conflict, earning the latter the honor of Erdtree Burial. The belligerents of said conflict are not confirmed; however, Godefroy's involvement may suggest that the remnants of the Golden Lineage were the attackers.

sections.heading: The Second Defense of Leyndell
sections.markdown:
During the Second Defense of Leyndell, Morgott, in the guise of Margit the Fell Omen, slaughtered many heroes in his defense of the Erdtree and engaged in conflict with Radahn.

Whether Morgott actually defeated Radahn is unclear, as his description as the mightiest hero of the demigods would suggest not. Regardless, while the walls of Leyndell did not fall, Radahn survived, and his forces were repelled. Alongside what were apparently Radahn's forces, soldiers of Godrick and Stormveil Castle also took part in the battle.

sections.heading: The Assault on Volcano Manor
sections.markdown: Said to have been the most appalling battle in the Shattering, the conflict took place on Mt. Gelmir, seemingly between Praetor Rykard's army and the forces of Leyndell. The squalid, the sick, and the blasphemous are said to have participated in this battle, which went on without end. The attackers brought the Jar Cannon to the assault; however, it was discovered that nobody knew how to use it. Most of the soldiers in Leyndell's army eventually became afflicted by Frenzy and seemingly resorted to cannibalism, consuming the bodies of the dead. Rykard's own men deserted him following this conflict, no longer able to abide the consequences of his blasphemy.

sections.heading: Godrick vs Malenia
sections.markdown: Scarcely deserving of being considered a balanced conflict on her journey to face Radahn in the Battle of Aeonia, Malenia and her Cleanrot Knights marched past Stormveil Castle, where Godrick the Grafted and his own forces had been cowering from the Red Lion general. Apparently, Godrick did something to insult Melania, sparking a fight between the pair. Godrick was defeated, and rather than choosing to die in battle, he begged Malenia for mercy. Godrick was spared, and Malenia pressed on to meet Radahn.

sections.heading: The Battle of Aeonia
sections.markdown: The final act of the Shattering was the Battle of Aeonia, a conflict between General Radahn and Malenia, Blade of Miquella. It occured in the area south of Sellia, Town of Sorcery in Caelid, in a region now known as the Swamp of Aeonia. Malenia and her army of Cleanrot Knights marched southward before arriving in Caelid, where they met Radahn's Redmane Knights in battle. The battle ended in a stalemate after Malenia unleashed her scarlet rot, driving the Redmane Knights to defeat. At the same time, their leader was infected with the rot, which drove Radahn into becoming a mindless beast.

sections.heading: Aftermath
sections.markdown: Ultimately, none of the Demigods succeeded in becoming Elden Lord, and they were abandoned by the Greater Will. Instead, the guidance of Grace was extended to the Tarnished, who were called to the Lands Between to claim the Great Runes, become Elden Lord, and restore the Golden Order.

sections.heading: *Nightreign*
sections.markdown:
The events of the Shattering in the alternate timeline are likely the same, though the aftermath is entirely different in comparison. In the aftermath of the civil war, a primordial cataclysm known as simply the Night and its harbingers Heolstor and the Nightlords emerged and descended on the Lands Between. As Marika's shattering of the Elden Ring and the Shattering had destroyed order itself, the Night, through the Night's Tide, began plunging the Lands Between into darkness and chaos, drawing forth all manner of monsters and beasts from different realms and eras as perpetual rain threatened to wash away everything.

As the world was alternated and consumed by the Night, the Golden Order ceased to exist. Queen Marika seemed to have disappeared completely from the Lands Between, as she and the Elden Ring are no longer prayed to, though a few churches remained standing. Meanwhile, the Erdtree itself had vanished entirely from the Lands Between, and its golden, radiant hues are no longer visible. Its disappearance, along with the Grace of Gold, prevented the Tarnished from being beckoned by its call to return. The fate of many of the demigods is unknown, but they presumably died out during the Shattering, while only very few, namely Morgott, Godrick and Mohg, were left alive. In response to the growing darkness, a group of warriors from other lands known as the Nightfarers chose to stay in the Limveld to slay the Nightlords and end the Night.

sections.markdown: The **Stranded Souls** are the spirits of nameless characters in Elden Ring and Elden Ring: Shadow of the Erdtree.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
Stranded Souls can be found throughout the Lands Between, offering short pieces of dialogue which serve to add context to the lore and story. These spirits are translucent, and they take on a variety of appearances based on the inhabitants of the Lands Between, such as commoners and Noble Sorcerers.

The Stranded Souls always face directly toward whatever it is they are speaking about.

- Localisation Notes

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: The **Sword Monuments** are unmarked locations found throughout the Lands Between in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown: The sword monuments are clusters of great stone swords verically embedded in the earth, often found near ancient battlegrounds. They were erected to memorialize important events in the history of the Lands Between, inscribed on the largest blades.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown: - The swords that are used in the Sword Monuments are strikingly similar to the Stone-Sheathed Sword, which may be transformed into either the Sword of Light or Sword of Darkness.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.markdown:
- Localization Notes
 - The two Liurnian Wars and the Routing of the Ancient Dragons are referred to as 戦役 (*Sen'eki*), which can be read "military campaign" and "battle", as well as "war."
 - The second line in the First Liurnian War monument says less ambiguously "red-haired Radagon becomes a hero." (赤髪のラダゴン、英雄となる, *Akagami no Radagon, eiyū to naru*.)
 - The "siege" of Caria Manor is referred to as 防衛戦 (*Kōjō-sen*) meaning "defensive battle", the same kanji used to refer to the First and Second Defenses of Leyndell.
 - Radahn less ambiguously is called "protector of Sellia" (サリアの護り, *Saria no mamori*) in the second line of the Starscourge Conflict monument.
 - The second line of the Routing of the Ancient Dragons monument says less specifically that Godwyn the Golden fought bravely or desperately, rather than "to the last." (黄金のゴッドウィン勇戦し, *Ougon no Goddowin yūsen shi*)
 - The second line of the First Defense of Leyndell monument says that the sovereign alliance "collapses from within and becomes defeated" or "becomes a defeated army." (内から瓦解し敗軍となる, *Uchi kara gakai shi haigun to naru*.)
